title.narrative: The ILO is able to influence regional agenda through key regional institutions including in the delivery of the 2030 Agenda

description.narrative:
In March 2023, during its 347th Session, the ILO Governing Body approved the ILO strategy for decent work in supply chains. It was based on the building blocks adopted by the Tripartite Working Group on Ensuring Decent Work in Supply Chains (June-July 2022). The Strategy was operationalized through the establishment of an action programme aimed at promoting decent work in supply chains.
In the current biennium, ILO supports the development of a strategy for the Asia-Pacific region to give effect to the ILO Strategy for Decent Work in Supply Chains. This strategy includes promoting policy coherence on the nexus between trade, investment, and decent work through a high-level regional policy forum and close engagement with multilateral organizations and international financial institutions. The ILO provides coherent advice to Member States on achieving decent work outcomes, foster strategies to promote the ratification and effective implementation of international labor standards, strengthen labor administration to ensure compliance with national labor laws, and support constituents in applying principles of responsible business conduct and due diligence throughout supply chains. Additionally, the strategy aims to enhance supply chain resilience by providing tools to upgrade skills, productivity, wages, and support for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).
